$comment: Offset profile for one exact LMU build. Everything address-shaped lives here,
not in code. Regenerate with `inactive-reset reanchor <old.bin> <new.bin>`.
Addresses are RVAs: add the module base, which is ASLR'd and must be read at
runtime. Never hardcode a base.
confidence:  E = established, multiple concurring references or direct proof
I = inferred from a single reference or by adjacency
U = unresolved; the value is STALE and must not be trusted

build.note: The 2026-08-11 patch did not bump the file version. Identify builds by hash, never by version.

$comment: Read these bytes at this RVA and compare before trusting anything else.
Bytes 12..15 are the disp32 of `MOV RAX,[RIP+x]` and change on any rebuild
that moves data, EVEN IF the function itself is identical. Compare the
first 12 bytes when deciding whether the FUNCTION changed.

arrayBase.note: Unanimous vote across 45 independent referencing instructions.

lateralSign.note: sign of this selects the lateral direction

pitState.note: watched after placement until it clears

pitFlag.note: mInPits. Published to shared memory by DynMan_FillScoring at 0x00CD987F. Also reachable as controller+0x2050 where controller = container+0x6F80 - the SAME byte the pit-entry/pit-exit handlers set and clear, which is why writing it is a complete operation and not half of one. See lapValidity.

countLapFlag.note: 0 count neither, 1 count lap but NOT time, 2 count lap and time. Recomputed only at the start/finish line. See lapValidity.

lapCountsNext.note: Latch consumed at the next start/finish crossing to decide countLapFlag. See lapValidity.

lapStartEt.note: Elapsed time the current lap started. Written by the promote block and by nothing else, which makes it the witness for whether a start/finish crossing was accepted as a lap completion at all. See lapValidity.

lapNumber.note: Lap counter. Incremented in the same handler as the promote block.

sector.note: Current sector index, zero-based, 0 -> 1 -> 2 -> 0. A start/finish crossing is accepted as a lap completion ONLY on the 2 -> 0 edge. Slot_Reset zeroes it, so a placement past the last sector line leaves the car arriving at the line reading 0 and the crossing is discarded. Writing 2 after placing fixes it. MEASURED against the running game 2026-08-12.

vehMotionState.note: [0..2] world vel, [3..5] local vel, [6..8] angular. Read to verify arrival; NEVER written.

$comment: Two different consumption patterns, and the difference is everything.
readLive    : the consumer dereferences this address on every evaluation,
so writing it takes effect immediately.
expandedOnce: read once at session start and exploded into derived flags.
Writing it mid-session does NOTHING. Write the derived flags.

flagRules.domain: 0 none, 1 penalties only, 2 penalties + full-course yellows, 3 all except DQ
flagRules.gates: the stop/go for speeding in the pit lane
flagRules.note: The REST setter clamps this to a floor of 1 and therefore CANNOT disable the penalty. A direct write can. Verified 2026-08-11.

config.note: Writing this mid-session has NO effect. Present for display only.

$derivedNote: These are marked readLive because the EVALUATOR dereferences them on every
evaluation -- they are the expansion OUTPUT, not the config input. That is
what makes them writable mid-session while the config byte above is not.

derivedFlags.note: NOT re-derived for this build by reanchor; the value is stale.
Gates 'Track Limits: Off Track - Lap Invalidated'. THIS is the one that matters.

trackLimits.initNote: Session init does `mov word ptr [0x03B36274], 0x0101`, setting 74 AND 75 together. The engine's own Disabled branch clears only 74, which is why 75 must be written by hand.

stewardPenalties.note: No direct readers found, which by the taxonomy above means it is expanded through a pointer. Derived state NOT located. Displayed, never written.

$comment: How the engine decides whether a lap counts and whether it is timed.
Reference only: nothing loads this section. MEASURED against the running
game on 2026-08-12, not inferred. Full account in docs/LAP_VALIDITY.md.
THE CAUSE of a placed car losing a lap is the SECTOR SEQUENCER, not any
lap-validity rule:
sector (+0x1CEA8, int32)  current sector, zero-based, 0 -> 1 -> 2 -> 0
A start/finish crossing is accepted as a lap completion only on the 2 -> 0
edge. Slot_Reset zeroes the sector, which is right when leaving the pits
and wrong once the tool has put the car mid-lap. A car placed past the
last sector line crosses no sector lines, arrives reading 0, and the
crossing is DISCARDED: lap counter, lapStartEt and countLapFlag all stay
put. Writing sector = 2 after placing fixes it; only final-sector
placements are affected. Writing 2 for an earlier placement was measured
to be harmless - the crossing is still accepted - though the engine does
not appear to move the sector backwards, so such a lap may carry no
meaningful sector splits.
SEPARATELY, whether an accepted lap is TIMED comes from:
countLapFlag  (+0x1CFF0, int32) the current lap: 0 neither, 1 lap but
not time, 2 lap and time
lapCountsNext (+0x1CFF4, byte)  latch for the lap about to start
lapStartEt    (+0x1CFF8, double) when the current lap started
At an accepted crossing the engine promotes countLapFlag from the latch,
then demotes it again if the session is not a race and pitFlag is set --
the out-lap rule. pitFlag was NOT the cause: it clears itself about 33 s
after a placement. Clearing it still guards a real but narrow race, since
a final-sector placement can reach the line in about ten seconds.
lapStartEt has exactly one writer, the promote block. That makes it the
only field that separates 'the handler ran and demoted' from 'the handler
never ran' -- which look identical in countLapFlag, and which is how the
first diagnosis of this went wrong.
Code sites are under functions.lapValidity, NOT here, because that is how
reanchor decides to re-derive an address by masked signature search rather
than by voting on referencing instructions, and these are code.
How the engine places a car. NOT settings -- measured behaviour.
In this build GetPitDestination (0x00D4C310) reads these from a MUTABLE
.data tunable block rather than from .rdata literals, so they are runtime
values that Studio 397 can retune without moving a single address.
`tunables` are therefore READ LIVE from the running process at placement
time. `fallback` is used only when a live read fails its range check --
which is what a relocated block looks like. If both fail, `place` refuses.
That way a retune needs no profile update at all, and a MOVE is an
ordinary reanchor.
yawOffsetDegrees is stored in DEGREES and converted at 0x00D4C531 by
0.01745329 (pi/180) before `oriOut[1] -= sign * value`. The fallback below
is the RADIAN equivalent, because that is the unit the model works in.

yawOffsetDegrees.note: 45.0 in the 44C3EE9C dump; was a 35 deg .rdata literal in 266D1AF6

fallback.$comment: Used ONLY when the live read fails its range check. Snapshot from LMU_runtime_44C3EE9C.bin, a runtime dump, so post-config.

ranges.$comment: A wrong RVA yields plausible floats, not a fault. These bounds turn that into a refusal. Deliberately wide: they reject nonsense, they do not second-guess Studio 397.

functions.$comment: Reference points for analysis. NOTHING in this project calls into LMU.

$comment: Instruction sites, not function entries -- the signature search does not
care which. Byte-exact unique matches in LMU_runtime_44C3EE9C.bin.
Nothing calls these; they exist so the next patch can re-locate the rule
instead of re-deriving it. A 'U' here blocks nothing: the placement fix
uses container offsets, which are layout and do not live in this section.

promoteAtStartFinish.note: cmp[+0x164],r13b / setnz / inc / mov[+0x160],eax / mov[+0x170],0 / mov word[+0x164],1. Displacements are from container+0x1CE90, so +0x160 is countLapFlag and +0x164 is the latch.

demoteWhenInPits.note: cmp[+0x8FD0],0 / jz / cmp[+0x160],2 / jnz / mov[+0x160],1. Reached only when the JBE on (session-10 <= 3) falls through, i.e. races are exempt from the out-lap rule.

invalidateNextLap.note: mov byte[+0x164],0 in the track-limits chokepoint - the 'This and next lap will not count' path. Separate from the pit-flag rule; listed so the two are not confused.

slotResetSetsPitFlag.note: mov byte[rcx+0x2050],1 with rcx = container+0x6F80; 0x6F80+0x2050 == 0x8FD0. In the helper at 0x00EB8CA0 that the 2026-08-11 patch extracted out of Slot_Reset - it was inline at 0x00D2A59A in the 266D1AF6 dump.

slotResetClearsPitFlag.note: mov word[rdi+0x8FD0],0 - the other Slot_Reset branch.
